comparison.objective: Extend a loose paint-roller pole to a marked length, relock its internal twist cam, and prove load retention; the candidate instead sets a gripper opening-stop screw, locks its jam nut without disturbing the setting, and cycles the gripper.
comparison.physical_skill: Both require bimanual counter-rotation and retention, but PR-1855 counter-twists and axially slides two tubes; the candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench seating and countertorque during locknut tightening.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1855 requires 93–95 cm length and under 2 mm shortening during a 50 N push; the candidate requires a retained 90° opening, limited drift, three repeated cycles, retained nuts, and released clearance.
comparison.reason: This is the closest record, but preserving a threaded adjustment while tightening its concentric jam nut and then verifying articulated cycles is meaningfully different from setting and load-testing a telescoping cam lock.
